QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_42

question.text: An SE Hariyali Foundation claims 500 hectares of wasteland restored. The SIA's sub-sample inspection finds 32% of the claimed area shows no visible restoration. The materiality question is:

answer.text: Whether the CEO will be upset
Whether the news media will notice

Whether 32% is statistically ≤ the confidence-interval, whether the 32% could be attributed to inspection-timing (off-season) or whether it is genuine overclaim — and whether the 32% gap is material for the SE's SROI and reporting integrity

explanation.text: The Logic: Materiality under SAS-500 is both quantitative (32% is a LARGE gap) and qualitative (overclaim goes to SE credibility). The SIA must assess statistical significance vs seasonal artefact vs genuine overclaim, then decide on qualified / adverse conclusion. The Trap: Options B, A, D are non-audit considerations. Cross-Exam Context: Overclaim-materiality analysis in III-A / III-C Compliance (regulatory materiality) and XV Research Analyst. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Schedule restoration inspections during growth season (post-monsoon in India, Sep-Nov). Inspecting in peak summer can falsely suggest non-restoration because grass has dried.
